pr_title: spanconfig: introduce factory to construct txn scoped SQLTranslators
pr_body:
The SQLTranslator is responsible for translating a tenant's SQL zone
config state to the implied KV span config state. It is used by the
Reconciler to issue updates to KV whenever a zone config or PTS record
changes. However, deletions corresponding to PTS-es being released or
tables being deleted aren't handeld by the Translator; instead, the
Reconciler identifies such cases and issues deletion requests to KV.

Previously, the Translator would create its own txn to read from
system.{zones,descriptors,protected_ts_records} when constructing span
config state, and the Reconciler would create and use a separate txns to
identify and generate the deleiton requests described above.

This isn't sound, because we aren't reconciling a snapshot of the SQL
state by using 3 different transactions here. In practice, when
working with "regular" span configurations, it just happened to be the
case that this wasn't a problem because of the way the code was
structured. We would check if we needed to construct a deletion by
trying to read a table descriptor corresponding to an ID before we
translated it, so there was no way for us to construct both a deletion
and an update for the same table in the same batch. Had the order of
operations been reversed, we would be susceptible to a race with a
concurrent table descriptor delete.

This is a real problem for system span configurations however. Think
protection timestamps written on the entire keyspace of a tenant.
Protected timestamp records that apply to the entire keyspace may be
deleted and re-written multiple times, unlike table descriptors which
can never be re-written after they've been deleted as in our previous
illustration. Thus, we may end up generating an update and a delete
for the same system span config target in the same batch. Instead of
trying to figure out which one actually applies, we instead eschew this
entirely by constructing span config state transactionally in the
Reconciler. Instead of using 3 different transactions like we were
before, we now work with a single transaction and use it for:

- Translating SQL state to span config state
- Constructing "regular" span config deletions if a table has been
dropped.
- Constructing system span config deletions

To do so, this patch changes  the SQLTranslator to be single-use and
transaction scoped.  We introduce a new SQLTranslatorFactory to bind
transactions and construct such a SQLTranslator in the Reconciler.
Every time the reconciler is processing a batch of updates from the
Watcher, it now constructs a fresh SQLTranslator.

Fixes #77828

Release justification: bug fixes and low-risk updates to new functionality.
Release note: None

comments: I'm not sure what the reasoning behind this check is https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/99c969102111beaa3025ba0046cdc0a83337fcba/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigstore/systemspanconfigstore.go#L179. Is it not possible for two consecutive cluster target records to be applied by the store?

I don't have a minimal reproduction yet but I have some sort of reproduction in the test I added - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/77726

The updates that are causing the node to crash are of the form:
```
[{target:{span:{Key:[] EndKey:[]} systemTarget:{sourceTenantID:{InternalValue:1} targetTenantID:{InternalValue:0} systemTargetType:2}} config:{RangeMinBytes:0 RangeMaxBytes:0 GCPolicy:{TTLSeconds:0 ProtectionPolicies:[] IgnoreStrictEnforcement:false} GlobalReads:false NumReplicas:0 NumVoters:0 Constraints:[] VoterConstraints:[] LeasePreferences:[] RangefeedEnabled:false ExcludeDataFromBackup:false}} 

{target:{span:{Key:[] EndKey:[]} systemTarget:{sourceTenantID:{InternalValue:1} targetTenantID:{InternalValue:0} systemTargetType:2}} config:{RangeMinBytes:0 RangeMaxBytes:0 GCPolicy:{TTLSeconds:0 ProtectionPolicies:[{ProtectedTimestamp:{WallTime:3 Logical:0 Synthetic:false} IgnoreIfExcludedFromBackup:false}] IgnoreStrictEnforcement:false} GlobalReads:false NumReplicas:0 NumVoters:0 Constraints:[] VoterConstraints:[] LeasePreferences:[] RangefeedEnabled:false ExcludeDataFromBackup:false}}]
```

This corresponds to a release and a protect being processed in the same batch of updates. This seems okay unless I'm missing some higher-level invariant that should be preventing this? Also isn't this reordering of updates being applied bad, the logs suggest that the Protect was called before the Release but the updates are ordered differently.

> This corresponds to a release and a protect being processed in the same batch of updates. This seems okay unless I'm missing some higher-level invariant that should be preventing this?

When I wrote this, I was following this invariant: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/99c969102111beaa3025ba0046cdc0a83337fcba/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfig.go#L208 We do something similar for "regular span configs" as well: 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/99c969102111beaa3025ba0046cdc0a83337fcba/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigstore/spanconfigstore.go#L414-L420

Do we know how this invariant enforced for regular span configs in the `Reconciler` and `KVSubscriber`?

@adityamaru and I looked at this together a bit, and seems like the real issue is the way we're constructing `Updates` to be passed in to the store. Specifically, we construct `SystemSpanConfigs` deletions using this list: 

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/99c969102111beaa3025ba0046cdc0a83337fcba/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigreconciler/reconciler.go#L416-L420

And we construct updates using the SQLTranslator: 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/99c969102111beaa3025ba0046cdc0a83337fcba/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigreconciler/reconciler.go#L422-L425

As the SQLTranslator creates its own transaction internally, these things are happening in separate transactions. This means we're susceptible to races like: 

```
Backup 1: Release()
Watcher: Notifies on entire keyspace. 
Reconciler: Filter missing update for entire keyspace
Backup 2: Protect()
Reconciler: Translate entire-keyspace, constructing an update 
--- panic
Watcher: Notifies on Entire keyspace (corresponding to the `Protect`)
```

----

I don't think we want to remove the duplication check in the `systemSpanConfigStore` and rely on the ordering of updates passed to it. Instead, we probably don't want to end up in this situation to begin with by only creating a transactional view of updates to apply to the store. There's actually a TODO that talks about this hazard:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/91563a5086e0628aa64288871ad3613f3edfb29e/pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigreconciler/reconciler.go#L406-L409

My proposal is to make it such that we can bind a transaction to the `SQLTranslator` and make it single use. Let's create a `SQLTranslatorFactory` that does this binding and pass it as a dependency to the `Reconciler`. 

----

This was on the `Reconciler` side of things -- I'm going to spend some time auditing the `KVSubscriber` side and make sure this check doesn't trip us up.

review_comments: Either leave a TODO here to return missing table IDs from the translator, or make that change. There's no reason for this to exist on the reconciler anymore -- the translator is also missing-table-aware.
Ditto re: TODO, the translator could adopt this responsibility easily instead of having the reconciler house this logic. This is easy now that the translator's txn scoped.
